precepts.text: To all that are carried away captives: build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them; take ye wives, and beget sons and daughters; and take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to husbands, that ye may be increased there, and not diminished. So Paul was not contradicting the Bible and telling anybody to reject work, education, marriage, or building. Increase even in Babylon.
precepts.point: Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth: mortify means to deaden. Fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence: sexual sins. And covetousness, which is idolatry: because when your god is your own flesh and you want to please that and only that, it is idolatry.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
Was Paul saying to reject the things on the earth, to hell with education, to hell with getting work? No. Jeremiah shows what the Lord told His people in captivity: “Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, unto all that are carried away captives, whom I have caused to be carried away from Jerusalem unto Babylon; Build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them.”

“Take ye wives, and beget sons and daughters”: get married and have children. “And take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to husbands, that they may bear sons and daughters”: pick good wives and good husbands for your children. “That ye may be increased there, and not diminished”: increased even there in Babylon.

So Paul was not contradicting the Bible. Seeking “those things which are above” does not mean rejecting work, education, marriage or building. It means putting to death the sins of the flesh, while still building houses, planting gardens and raising families even in captivity.

precepts.text: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations: teach the Israelites scattered in all nations. That is the prophecy, and that is why IUIC travels to all these countries and just carried out one of the biggest worldwide blitzes: to bring back our people to who they are.
precepts.point: And I will bring you again into the place whence I caused you to be carried away captive: that is Jerusalem. That is our land. Everything you see here is temporary. You already know the end of the movie; you win. So why are you bugging out? Last week the Bishop was teaching how some of us turn to liquor to deal with the hatred and the trauma. You have to expect the hatred; the problem is you are dying to be loved by people who will never love you.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

precepts.why:
“And I will be found of you, saith the Lord: and I will turn away your captivity, and I will gather you from all the nations”. Why does it say from all nations? This is for the Israelite who says there is no Israelite in Africa. No matter where you go on the planet, you are going to find some Israelite; that is why he says all nations, “and from all the places whither I have driven you”.

That is why Christ said, “Go ye therefore, and teach all nations”. Teach the Israelites, because we were scattered in all nations. That is the prophecy. And no matter where we are, we are going to be hated.

That is why IUIC travels to all these countries: to bring our people back to who they are and tell them they are the Israelites. That is why we just had one of the biggest worldwide blitzes, because we understand the scripture and we follow it. As John saw, Christ redeemed us to God by his blood out of every kindred, tongue, people and nation, and the Lord will bring us again into the place whence he caused us to be carried away captive.

precepts.text: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake: Christ himself said it, so why am I surprised when they hate me? But he that endureth to the end shall be saved. When they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: for verily I say unto you, ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come. We are not going to be able to wake every single Israelite before Christ comes back; that is what he is saying.
precepts.point: And I will bring you again into the place whence I caused you to be carried away captive: that is Jerusalem. That is our land. Everything you see here is temporary. You already know the end of the movie; you win. So why are you bugging out? Last week the Bishop was teaching how some of us turn to liquor to deal with the hatred and the trauma. You have to expect the hatred; the problem is you are dying to be loved by people who will never love you.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

precepts.why:
Jeremiah says the Lord will gather us from all the nations whither he has driven us, and in all those nations we are hated. Christ said so himself: “And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake”. If Christ, the black Messiah himself, said I am going to be hated of all men, why am I surprised when they hate me? That shows the Christians are not reading this Bible. “but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.”

“But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come.” We are not going to be able to cover the whole earth. We will not wake up every single Israelite before Christ comes back; that is what he is saying.

But the Lord will “bring you again into the place whence I caused you to be carried away captive”: Israel, Jerusalem, our land. Everything you see here is temporary. It is a movie, and you already know the end: you win. So why are you bugging out? Some of us turn to liquor and alcohol to deal with the hatred and the trauma. You have to expect the hatred. The problem is you are dying to be loved by people who are never going to love you.

precepts.text: Ahab and Zedekiah prophesied lies in my name and committed adultery with their neighbours' wives, and the king of Babylon roasted them in the fire.
precepts.point: They have thrown down thine altars and slain thy prophets, and I, even I only, am left. Israel's rulers killed the prophets who taught against them. The same people mock the purple and gold today.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Susanna says wickedness came from Babylon from ancient judges, “such as the Lord spake of”. Where did the Lord speak of it? In Jeremiah, to “all ye of the captivity, whom I have sent from Jerusalem to Babylon”.

“Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, of Ahab the son of Kolaiah, and of Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah, which prophesy a lie unto you in my name; Behold, I will deliver them into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon; and he shall slay them before your eyes”. And the captivity would curse by their names: “The Lord make thee like Zedekiah and like Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire”. He cooked them to death.

Why? “Because they have committed villany in Israel, and have committed adultery with their neighbours’ wives, and have spoken lying words in my name, which I have not commanded them”. That is what your pastors be doing. “even I know, and am a witness, saith the Lord.”

These were the wicked leaders among the people, false prophets instead of the true ones they persecuted. The Pharisees did the exact same thing when Rome ruled: ancient evil from Babylon, from the elders.

precepts.text: Build houses and plant gardens and eat the fruit of them; that is the wealth the Most High teaches.
precepts.point: We have to be retaught what wealth is: build houses, dwell in them, plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them, and learn to provide for ourselves.

note.label: Genesis 13: The Peacemaker and the Promise

precepts.why:
“Abram was very rich in cattle, in silver, and in gold.” When the scriptures speak of our forefathers being rich, it is not carnal wealth. Abram was rich in livestock, land, and the things that take care of a family; that is true wealth.

We have to be retaught what wealth is: “Build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them.” Build houses and plant gardens and eat the fruit of them, and learn to provide for ourselves. That is the wealth the Most High teaches.

precepts.text: Even in the seventy years under Babylon the Lord said build ye houses, plant gardens, take wives, and beget sons and daughters, that ye may be increased there and not diminished; captivity was never a command to stop building your house.
precepts.point: It is important for us to build our legacy and pass it down; that is one of the things we lack in Israel today. Some of us use captivity as an excuse not to better ourselves or build, but that is not what the scriptures say: get the job, further your education, do more for yourself, your family, and the body. Building up your house also means spiritually building it, teaching your wife and children.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
Captivity was never a command to stop building your house. Even in the seventy years under Babylon the Lord said: “Build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them; Take ye wives, and beget sons and daughters; and take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to husbands, that they may bear sons and daughters; that ye may be increased there, and not diminished.”

Some of us use captivity as an excuse not to better ourselves or build, but that is not what the scriptures say. Build houses, plant gardens, take wives, beget sons and daughters, be increased and not diminished: build your legacy and pass it down, even here.

precepts.text: After seventy years at Babylon the Most High promised to visit his people and bring them back to their place.
precepts.point: Cyrus was one of the first kings of Persia, and the Most High used him to give the order to rebuild Jerusalem. His coming was prophesied long before by name.

note.label: Ezra 1: Cyrus Stirred Up to Send Israel Home

precepts.why:
Ezra says this happened “that the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled”. This is that word: “For thus saith the Lord, That after seventy years be accomplished at Babylon I will visit you, and perform my good word toward you, in causing you to return to this place.”

After seventy years at Babylon the Most High promised to visit His people and bring them back to their place. So in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia He stirred up the spirit of Cyrus, and the proclamation went out through all his kingdom to build Him a house at Jerusalem. The return home was the Most High performing His good word, exactly as Jeremiah had spoken it.

precepts.text: Seek the peace of the city where you are carried away captive and pray for it, for in its peace you shall have peace, which is why Mordecai kept the king safe.
precepts.point: The thing was known to Mordecai who told it to Esther the queen, and Esther told the king in Mordecai's name, and when it was searched out and found true the two were both hanged on a tree, and it was written in the book of the chronicles before the king. Israel wrote down our history and our chronicles, and this deed of Mordecai's would later help our whole nation.

note.label: Esther 2: Esther Made Queen and Mordecai Uncovers the Plot

precepts.why:
Two of the king's chamberlains “were wroth, and sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus”, plotting a coup, and “the thing was known to Mordecai, who told it unto Esther the queen; and Esther certified the king thereof in Mordecai’s name.” Mordecai was a captive in Persia, yet he kept the king safe.

That is what the Lord had told the captives to do: “seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the Lord for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace.” The Lord caused them to be carried there; a coup against the king was no peace for the city, and no peace for Israel in it. So Mordecai exposed it.

“when inquisition was made of the matter, it was found out; therefore they were both hanged on a tree: and it was written in the book of the chronicles before the king.” Israel wrote down our history and our chronicles, and this deed of Mordecai's, written in the king's book, would later help our whole nation. In the peace of the city, Israel had peace.

precepts.text: Be subject to the higher powers, for the powers that be are ordained of God; whoever resists the ordinance resists God, but rulers are a terror only to the evil, not to good works.
precepts.point: They are to take wives and beget sons and daughters, take wives for their sons and husbands for their daughters, that they may be increased and not diminished, and seek the peace of the city where He caused them to be carried away, for in the peace thereof they shall have peace.

note.label: Jeremiah 29: The Letter to the Captives

precepts.why:
The Most High told the captives to build houses and dwell in them, plant gardens, take wives, and seek the peace of the city where he caused them to be carried away, and pray to the Lord for it, “for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace.” Paul gives the same instruction to a people living under another power: “Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God.”

Babylon was the higher power over the captives, and it was the Lord that caused them to be carried there. “Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation.” To fight the captivity was to fight what God ordained.

“For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil.” So the captives could buy homes, plant gardens, marry, be increased and not diminished, and have peace in the city, so long as they did that which is good: “do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same”.

precepts.text: A man's goings are of the Lord, who put the spirit on man to go out and teach the people.
precepts.point: The Most High never comes down here Himself to speak to the people; He speaks through His servants the prophets.

note.label: Jeremiah 29: The Letter to the Captives

precepts.why:
The Lord sent his words to the people “by my servants the prophets, rising up early and sending them”. The Most High never comes down here himself to speak to the people; he speaks through his servants the prophets. Solomon shows who sends them: “Man’s goings are of the Lord; how can a man then understand his own way?”

A man's goings are of the Lord. It is the Lord that puts the spirit on a man to go out and teach the people. The prophets today are the ones going out teaching on the corners every Sabbath and seven days a week, and their goings are of him. So it behooves us to follow God's laws when we hear them, because those that would not hear the prophets he sent were made like vile figs, a curse and a reproach among all the nations.

precepts.text: Israel is the Lord's servant, Jacob whom He chose, the seed of Abraham, taken from the ends of the earth; it is not all people.
precepts.point: The Most High never comes down here Himself to speak to the people; He speaks through His servants the prophets.

note.label: Jeremiah 29: The Letter to the Captives

precepts.why:
The servants the Lord sends are taken out of one people: “But thou, Israel, art my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend.” Israel is the Lord's servant, Jacob whom he chose, the seed of Abraham. It is not all people.

“Thou whom I have taken from the ends of the earth, and called thee from the chief men thereof, and said unto thee, Thou art my servant; I have chosen thee, and not cast thee away.” The prophets that rose up early to warn Judah were of this servant, and so are the ones teaching on the corners today. Even after the sword, the famine and the pestilence, and being driven among all the nations, Israel is chosen and not cast away.

precepts.text: Woe to the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of His pasture; He will visit upon them the evil of their doings.
precepts.point: They would become a curse, the Lord make thee like Zedekiah and like Ahab whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire, because they committed villainy in Israel, committed adultery with their brothers' wives, and spoke lying words in His name.

note.label: Jeremiah 29: The Letter to the Captives

precepts.why:
Ahab the son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah prophesied a lie in the Lord's name, and he delivered them to Nebuchadnezzar to be slain before the captives' eyes. The Lord had already spoken against men like them: “Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture!”

“Ye have scattered my flock, and driven them away, and have not visited them: behold, I will visit upon you the evil of your doings, saith the Lord.” The pastors that feed his people and scatter them instead get the evil of their own doings visited upon them. Ahab and Zedekiah, roasted in the fire by the king of Babylon and made a curse by all the captivity of Judah, are that woe carried out.

precepts.text: He heard the prophets that prophesy lies in His name, saying I have dreamed, and there were consequences for it.
precepts.point: They would become a curse, the Lord make thee like Zedekiah and like Ahab whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire, because they committed villainy in Israel, committed adultery with their brothers' wives, and spoke lying words in His name.

note.label: Jeremiah 29: The Letter to the Captives

precepts.why:
The Lord says of Ahab and Zedekiah, “even I know, and am a witness”. He had heard them: “I have heard what the prophets said, that prophesy lies in my name, saying, I have dreamed, I have dreamed.”

They spoke lying words in his name, which he had not commanded them, committed villainy in Israel, and committed adultery with their brothers' wives. He heard every word of it, and there were consequences for it: they were slain before the captives' eyes, and their names became a curse, “The Lord make thee like Zedekiah and like Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire”.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

precepts.why:
“And ye shall seek me, and find me, when ye shall search for me with all your heart.” That's what's happening right now: our people are seeking, and we are finding the Lord.

“And I will be found of you, saith the Lord: and I will turn away your captivity, and I will gather you from all the nations, and from all the places whither I have driven you, saith the Lord; and I will bring you again into the place whence I caused you to be carried away captive.” So God said he's going to gather us from all the nations, and bring us again into the place which he caused us to be carried away captive from. Captive.
